sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS EASTERN CO
sections.text: ...MIDDLE MS VALLEY/LOWER OH VALLEY TO SOUTHEAST STATES... STRONG/POTENTIALLY SEVERE TSTMS WILL BE ONGOING ACROSS THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY/LOWER OH VALLEY AT THE BEGINNING OF THE PERIOD...ON THE NOSE OF A VEERING 40+ KT LOW LEVEL JET...AND IN THE PRESENCE OF A CONVECTIVELY AIDED MID LEVEL IMPULSE AND/OR ONE OR MORE MCV/S AND BELT OF WEST-NORTHWESTERLY 40+ KT MID LEVEL FLOW. THE LOW LEVEL JET WILL TEND TO WEAKEN BY LATE MORNING/EARLY AFTERNOON...BUT WITH A RESIDUALLY MOIST/DIURNALLY DESTABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER...AND A STRONG INSTABILITY FEED FROM THE WEST-SOUTHWEST...MCS MAINTENANCE AND/OR REJUVENATION SEEMS LIKELY INTO THE AFTERNOON ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF EARLY DAY ACTIVITY. THIS WOULD MOST LIKELY OCCUR ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE LOWER OH RIVER/TN VALLEYS. SEVERE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO WILL BE POSSIBLE...BUT A POTENTIAL CORRIDOR/SWATH OF WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE MAIN HAZARD. LIMITED CONFIDENCE IN EARLY DAY CONVECTIVE DETAILS PRECLUDES A CATEGORICAL MODERATE RISK AT THIS TIME...BUT AN UPGRADE IS A POSSIBILITY WITH SUBSEQUENT OUTLOOKS...MOST LIKELY ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE LOWER OH/TN VALLEYS TO THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIANS. OTHER TSTMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP AND DIURNALLY UPSWING I

sections.title: MO VALLEY/PLAINS/CORN BELT
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF THE MORNING MCS/S...RISING HEIGHTS/WARMING ALOFT WILL GRADUALLY OCCUR ACROSS THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN PLAINS. WITH A WEAKENING/RESIDUAL UPPER LOW OVER THE DAKOTAS...INITIAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT MAY DIURNALLY OCCUR ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL PLAINS/ADJACENT CORN BELT ALONG A NORTHWEST-SOUTHEAST ORIENTED SURFACE TROUGH/INSTABILITY AXIS. FARTHER SOUTH ACROSS PORTIONS OF MO/EASTERN KS...DETAILS AT THIS TIME ARE ESPECIALLY COMPLICATED BY NUMEROUS EARLY DAY TSTMS/POTENTIAL CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW...IN ADDITION TO GRADUALLY WARMING TEMPERATURES ALOFT/LIMITED FORCING ON THE LARGE SCALE. NEVERTHELESS...ON THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF EARLY DAY ACTIVITY AND/OR ALONG A RESIDUAL FRONTAL ZONE/OUTFLOW...AT LEAST ISOLATED STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS SHOULD REDEVELOP BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING ACROSS THE LOWER MO VALLEY INCLUDING PORTIONS OF MO/EASTERN KS. AMPLE POTENTIAL INSTABILITY AND MODERATE VERTICAL SHEAR WOULD CONDITIONALLY SUPPORT SUPERCELLS. A MODEST LOW LEVEL JET/RESIDUAL BELT OF MODERATE WESTERLY ALOFT WOULD SUPPORT THE EASTWARD DEVELOPMENT OF ONE OR MORE STRONG CLUSTERS THROUGH THE EVENING/NIGHT WITH AT LEAST AN ISOLATED/CONTINUING SEVERE THREAT POSSIBLE TOWARD THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY/LOWER OH

sections.title: EASTERN CO/SOUTH CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: AS THE UPPER RIDGE BUILDS OVER THE REGION...RISING HEIGHTS/WARMING TEMPERATURES ALOFT WILL OCCUR ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. A LESSER SEVERE THREAT IS EXPECTED AS COMPARED TO MONDAY...BUT IT APPEARS A LATER AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING MOISTURE SURGE MAY RESULT IN ISOLATED TSTM DEVELOPMENT BY EARLY EVENING ALONG THE CO FRONT RANGE. A FEW OTHER TSTMS COULD ALSO DEVELOP ALONG/JUST NORTH OF THE SURFACE FRONT ACROSS FAR SOUTHWEST KS INTO THE OK PANHANDLE AS HOT TEMPERATURES ERODE THE CAP. IN EITHER CASE...MODERATE MID LEVEL FLOW WOULD CONDITIONALLY SUPPORT A FEW SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF HAIL/PERHAPS STRONG WIND GUSTS. ..GUYER/GRAMS.. 06/16/2009

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PARTS OF EASTERN CO
sections.text: ...MID MS VALLEY INTO KY/TN TODAY... MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY SHOWS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH TRACKING EASTWARD ACROSS MO...WITH AN ASSOCIATED LARGE MCS PRODUCING SCATTERED SEVERE WEATHER. THIS FEATURE WILL MOVE ACROSS THE MID MS VALLEY TODAY WHILE THE THUNDERSTORM CLUSTER MOVES EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD INTO PARTS OF IL/KY/TN. RELATIVELY STRONG WINDS ALOFT ACROSS THIS REGION...COUPLED WITH SIGNIFICANT MESOSCALE ORGANIZATION IN MCS SUGGESTS A CONTINUED THREAT OF LOCALLY SEVERE STORMS THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAY. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FINALLY WEAKEN AFTER SUNSET OVER THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS. DAMAGING WINDS ARE LIKELY TO BE THE MAIN THREAT.

sections.title: NORTHERN OK/SOUTHERN KS THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: UPSTREAM OF THIS AREA...THE UPPER RIDGE IS FORECAST TO BUILD ACROSS THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON. THIS WILL TEND TO WARM THE MID LEVELS AND INCREASE THE CAPPING INVERSION ACROSS PARTS OF TX/OK. NEVERTHELESS...THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY LEFT FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION EXTENDS ACROSS NORTHERN OK AND MAY BE THE FOCUS FOR ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT BY LATE AFTERNOON. HOT TEMPERATURES AND AMPLE LOW LEVEL MOISTURE WILL YIELD HIGH CAPE VALUES AND SUGGEST THAT ANY STORM THAT CAN BE SUSTAINED WILL LIKELY BE SEVERE.

sections.title: EASTERN SD INTO EASTERN KS/WESTERN MO
sections.text: EARLY MORNING VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS BACK EDGE OF CLOUD SHIELD EXTENDING FROM WEAK UPPER LOW OVER ND TO NEAR OMA...THEN SOUTHWARD TOWARD TUL. STRONG HEATING WILL OCCUR ALONG AND WEST OF THE CLOUD SHIELD...BUT UPPER RIDGING IS ALSO FORECAST TO OCCUR. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS WILL DEVELOP ALONG THIS CORRIDOR AROUND PEAK HEATING AND PERSIST FOR A FEW HOURS BEFORE WEAKENING. SUFFICIENT WESTERLY FLOW ALOFT AND EFFECTIVE DEEP LAYER SHEAR VALUES SUPPORT A RISK OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. FURTHER REFINEMENT OF THIS PART OF THE OUTLOOK WILL OCCUR THROUGH THE DAY AS FOCI FOR INITIATION AND EXTENT OF DESTABILIZATION BEHIND MCS OVER MO BECOME MORE CLEAR.

sections.title: EASTERN CO

sections.title: DAKOTAS
sections.text: CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK AND 5% TORNADO PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN EXTENDED NWWD INTO S-CNTRL ND TO ACCOUNT FOR ONGOING STORMS FROM VICINITY OF DEEP-LAYER LOW NW MBG SEWD ALONG TROUGH AXIS. HERE...THE COMBINATION OF 60+ F DEWPOINTS AND STEEPENING LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES ARE CONTRIBUTING TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WITH MLCAPE RANGING FROM AROUND 1000 J/KG NEAR SURFACE LOW TO 2000-2500 J/KG OVER SERN SD. RICH SOURCE OF VERTICAL VORTICITY NEAR THE LOW AND ATTENDANT SURFACE TROUGH COUPLED WITH THE STEEP LOW LEVEL-LAPSE RATES AND 0-3 KM CAPE AOB 150 J/KG WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF ROTATING STORMS CAPABLE OF TORNADOES AND HAIL INTO THIS EVENING.

sections.title: SRN OH/TN VALLEYS
sections.text: BOWING MCS MOVING INTO CNTRL KY AND MIDDLE TN AS OF 1930Z IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE EWD/SEWD THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING AT 35-45 KT...DRIVEN BY INFLUX OF A MOIST LOW-LEVEL AIR MASS AND SUSTAINED 50+ KT REAR INFLOW JET. LATEST MESOANALYSIS INDICATES A SLIGHTLY COOLER AIR MASS IN PLACE OVER CNTRL/ERN KY INTO ERN TN WHICH MAY TEND TO SUPPORT A MORE SEWD MOVEMENT OF SYSTEM AND/OR PREFERRED DEVELOPMENT ALONG IT/S SRN FLANK ACROSS SRN TN. WHILE SOME HAIL AND PERHAPS A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO ARE POSSIBLE...DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN THE PRIMARY SEVERE WEATHER THREAT WITH THE MCS AS IT MOVES INTO THE CUMBERLAND PLATEAU REGION.

sections.title: ERN PARTS OF KS/OK INTO THE OZARK PLATEAU
sections.text: SURFACE OBSERVATIONS AND VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY INDICATE WRN EXTENSION OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY REMNANT FROM KY/TN MCS RETREATING NWD THROUGH N-CNTRL/NERN OK AND FAR NWRN AR. GIVEN THAT MIDLEVEL RIDGE AND RESULTANT CAP IS CURRENTLY BUILDING OVER THE CNTRL/SRN PLAINS IN WAKE OF SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING THROUGH THE MID MS VALLEY...SEVERE THREAT IS CONDITIONAL ON STORM DEVELOPMENT AND SUSTENANCE. 18Z RUC REMAINS MOST AGGRESSIVE IN DEVELOPING STORMS INVOF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY OVER SERN KS INTO SWRN MO BETWEEN 16/21Z-17/00Z...WHEREAS THE 12Z RUNS OF THE NAM-WRF...GFS AND 4 KM WRF-NMM ALL SUGGEST AN INCREASING LIKELIHOOD AFTER 17/00Z AS LLJ STRENGTHENS OVER THE SRN PLAINS. AIR MASS REMAINS QUITE MOIST WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER 70S. WHEN COUPLED WITH THE STRONG DAYTIME HEATING AND STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...ENVIRONMENT IS MODERATE TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE WITH MLCAPE OF 2500-3500 J/KG. THIS INSTABILITY COINCIDES WITH 40-50 KT MIDLEVEL WLY WINDS PER AREA PROFILERS...RESULTING IN SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS SHOULD STORMS INITIATE AND BECOME SUSTAINED. LARGE HAIL WOULD BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE WEATHER HAZARD THOUGH TORNADOES ARE POSSIBLE WITH ANY STORMS THAT FAVORABLY INTERACT WITH OUTFL

sections.title: CO FRONT RANGE
sections.text: CATEGORICAL SLIGHT RISK AND 15% HAIL PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN REMOVED FROM AREA. TRENDS IN SURFACE OBSERVATIONAL DATA INDICATE BOUNDARY LAYER SLOWLY DRYING WITH DEWPOINTS FALLING THROUGH THE 40S. WHILE TSTMS STILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING...IT APPEARS THAT THE MARGINAL CONVECTIVE INSTABILITY SHOULD TEND TO LIMIT A MORE ORGANIZED SEVERE WEATHER THREAT. NONETHELESS...SOME HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY OF THE MORE INTENSE STORMS. ..MEAD.. 06/16/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1142 AM CDT TUE JUN 16 2009/
